note: Page recipes: the single source for recipe.mjs and LAYOUT-RULES.md. Edit here, then run recipe.mjs check.

recipes.name: Marketing landing page
recipes.use_when: One page that persuades a visitor from a campaign or search to take one action: buy, sign up, book or ask.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: In 3 seconds say what it is, who it is for and what to do: one headline, one sentence, one primary button and one image of the result.
sections.avoid: A generic claim like "the best platform", three buttons, and a stock photo that shows nothing.

sections.job: Show 4 to 6 real names the visitor trusts, right under the hero, before they doubt the claim.
sections.avoid: Invented or blurred logos, or a grid so big that it becomes the page.

sections.job: Name 3 outcomes the visitor gets, each with a short title and one sentence in the words of the audience.
sections.avoid: Listing features of the product instead of what changes for the visitor.

sections.job: Show the path from now to result in 3 numbered steps, so the action feels small.
sections.avoid: More than 4 steps, or steps that describe the product internals.

sections.job: Show the product or the result in use with one real screenshot or photo and a caption that says what to look at.
sections.avoid: A decorative mockup with lorem ipsum inside.

sections.job: Put a quote with a name, role and photo next to the doubt it removes, with one number when there is one.
sections.avoid: Anonymous praise such as "Great product!" that anyone could have written.

sections.job: Answer "how much?" with the plans or a starting price and what is included, before the visitor leaves to find out.
sections.avoid: Hiding the price behind "contact us" when the offer is a standard one.

sections.job: Answer the 5 to 7 doubts that stop the action, in the order of how often they come up.
sections.avoid: Questions the company wants to answer instead of the ones visitors ask.

sections.job: Repeat the same primary action once more, with the promise and the lowest-risk wording, after the visitor has the whole story.
sections.avoid: A different action than the hero, or three choices at the end.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: SaaS product home
recipes.use_when: The public home of a software product: it must explain a tool that is not obvious from a photo, and move the visitor to a trial or a demo.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Say which job the tool does and for whom, with a real screenshot of the main screen beside one headline and a "start free" or "book a demo" button.
sections.avoid: A dashboard illustration with fake charts and a headline made of buzzwords.

sections.job: Show the customers a buyer would recognise, in one row, so trust comes before the feature list.
sections.avoid: Logos of tools you integrate with, presented as if they were customers.

sections.job: Show the 4 to 6 capabilities that decide the purchase, each tile with a screenshot detail and one line of what it saves.
sections.avoid: A tile for every feature of the product: the visitor reads none.

sections.job: Let a visitor find their own case with 3 roles or jobs, each with its outcome and a link to the detail.
sections.avoid: Use cases written as company segments the visitor does not recognise themselves in.

sections.job: Remove the "will it work with my tools?" doubt by showing the 8 to 12 integrations that matter.
sections.avoid: Showing 60 logos where only 10 are real integrations.

sections.job: Back the claim with 3 or 4 measured numbers, each with what it counts and the period.
sections.avoid: Round numbers without a source or a unit.

sections.job: Show a customer with name, role and company who describes the result they got in their own numbers.
sections.avoid: A quote about how "easy" the tool is, with no result in it.

sections.job: Show the plans in a table of 3 columns with one highlighted, the billing toggle and what is free.
sections.avoid: Four plans with 20 rows of features, so no plan can be chosen.

sections.job: Settle the buyer's risk questions with 3 facts: where data lives, who can see it and the certifications held.
sections.avoid: Claiming certifications that are not held, or a shield icon with no fact beside it.

sections.job: Answer the trial, billing, cancel and data questions in short answers with a link when more is needed.
sections.avoid: Answers that say "contact sales" to every question.

sections.job: Repeat the trial or demo action with the first step visible, such as an email field.
sections.avoid: A second, different button that competes with the first.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Pricing page
recipes.use_when: A page whose only job is to let a visitor pick a plan and start, or understand why it costs what it costs.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Say in one headline what is being priced and add the billing toggle, so the plans below show the right price.
sections.avoid: A hero with an image: the visitor came for the price.

sections.job: Show 3 plans side by side, the recommended one highlighted, each with a price, 5 to 7 inclusions and one button.
sections.avoid: Four or more plans, or every button filled in the same color.

sections.job: Let the visitor switch between monthly and yearly and show the saving as a number.
sections.avoid: Showing the yearly price per month without saying it is billed yearly.

sections.job: Give the visitor who needs detail one table of features by plan, with the plan names fixed at the top.
sections.avoid: A table of 40 rows with a tick in every cell.

sections.job: Remove the fear of paying with 3 facts such as a refund period, cancel any time and no card to start.
sections.avoid: Guarantee text in small grey print under the button.

sections.job: Show one customer who says the price was worth it, with the plan they use.
sections.avoid: Quotes that praise the product and say nothing about the cost.

sections.job: Answer the billing questions: taxes, invoices, upgrades, cancel, refunds and what happens to the data.
sections.avoid: Pricing answers that depend on "it depends".

sections.job: Offer the same start action again and a way to talk to someone for a custom plan.
sections.avoid: Ending the page after the FAQ with no action.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: About / company page
recipes.use_when: A page that lets a stranger decide whether to trust the people behind the product or service.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: State in one sentence what the company does and why it exists, next to a real photo of the people or the place.
sections.avoid: A mission statement full of "innovative" and "passionate" with a stock photo.

sections.job: Tell in 3 short paragraphs how it started, the problem it saw and what changed since.
sections.avoid: A history that lists dates and says nothing about why anyone should care.

sections.job: Name 3 values as behaviours the customer can see, each with a proof in one line.
sections.avoid: Six abstract words such as "integrity" with no example.

sections.job: Give 3 or 4 verifiable figures: years, customers served, projects delivered.
sections.avoid: Vanity numbers with no unit or date.

sections.job: Show the people with a real photo, name and role, so a visitor knows who they will deal with.
sections.avoid: Cartoon avatars, or a team grid with no roles.

sections.job: Show 4 to 6 milestones in order when the history is part of the trust.
sections.avoid: A timeline of every product release.

sections.job: End with one next step that fits a curious visitor: contact, see the work or join the team.
sections.avoid: Three equal buttons for three different goals.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Contact page
recipes.use_when: A page where a visitor with a question or a request reaches a person with the least effort.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Say who answers and how fast, in one line, so the visitor trusts the form.
sections.avoid: A decorative hero image that pushes the form below the first screen.

sections.job: Collect the message with name, email and message only, one button and a clear promise of the reply time.
sections.avoid: Ten required fields, a captcha puzzle, or a button that says "Submit".

sections.job: Give the other ways to reach the company: email, phone with hours and the address, each one a link.
sections.avoid: A phone number as an image, or hours that are not stated.

sections.job: For a business with a place, show where it is with an interactive map and the address as text.
sections.avoid: A map with no address in text, so it cannot be copied.

sections.job: Answer the 3 questions that most contacts ask, so those people do not need the form.
sections.avoid: An FAQ longer than the form.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Blog index
recipes.use_when: The list of articles of a site: lets a reader find something worth reading and subscribe.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Say what the blog is about and for whom in one line, with a search field if there are more than 30 posts.
sections.avoid: A large hero that pushes the posts below the first screen.

sections.job: Put the one post to read first at the top with its image, title and a two-line summary.
sections.avoid: Three featured posts that compete for attention.

sections.job: Offer 4 to 7 topics as tabs or chips, with the active one marked, so a reader can narrow down.
sections.avoid: A tag cloud of 40 tags.

sections.job: List posts as cards with image, title, 2 lines of summary, date and reading time, all with the same image ratio.
sections.avoid: Cards with different heights and no date.

sections.job: Let the reader continue with numbered pages or a "load more" button that keeps the position.
sections.avoid: Infinite scroll with no way to reach the footer.

sections.job: Offer the subscription once, with what the reader gets and how often.
sections.avoid: A pop-up before the reader has read anything.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Article page
recipes.use_when: One article, guide or post read from start to end.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Give the title, a one-line summary, author, date and reading time, so the reader decides to stay.
sections.avoid: A title in three font sizes, or no date.

sections.job: Show one cover image that belongs to the article, with an aspect ratio of 16:9 and alt text.
sections.avoid: A stock image that says nothing about the topic.

sections.job: Make the text easy to read: 45 to 75 characters per line, body size, headings every few paragraphs.
sections.avoid: Full-width text at 1280px, which is over 120 characters per line.

sections.job: For a long article, show the table of contents with the current section marked.
sections.avoid: A table of contents that does not follow the scroll.

sections.job: Say who wrote it with a photo, a line of credentials and a link to more of their work.
sections.avoid: A bio of five lines about the author's hobbies.

sections.job: Offer 3 articles on the same topic to continue reading.
sections.avoid: Related posts that are only the latest posts.

sections.job: Close with a single subscribe action that fits the topic just read.
sections.avoid: A pop-up covering the text while it is being read.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Docs / reference page
recipes.use_when: A page of documentation where a reader looks something up or follows steps to do a task.

sections.job: Offer search first, then the version and the link back to the product.
sections.avoid: Search hidden behind an icon on desktop.

sections.job: Show the whole tree of the docs, with the current page marked and the section opened.
sections.avoid: A tree three levels deep, closed by default.

sections.job: Give one answer per page: a title, a short intro, steps or a table, and a result the reader can check.
sections.avoid: Several topics on one page with no headings.

sections.job: Show runnable code with a copy button, the language and the expected output.
sections.avoid: Code in an image or without the imports.

sections.job: List the headings of the page on the right with the current one marked.
sections.avoid: A list longer than the page.

sections.job: Ask "was this helpful?" with yes or no and one optional comment.
sections.avoid: A feedback form of five questions.

sections.job: Link the previous and the next page by title, so the reader can follow the order.
sections.avoid: Links named "previous" and "next" with no titles.

recipes.name: Portfolio case study
recipes.use_when: One project of a designer, developer or studio, told as a problem, a process and a result.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Name the project, the client, your role and the year, over the best image of the result.
sections.avoid: A title that is only the client name, with no role or result.

sections.job: Give the facts in 4 cells: role, duration, tools and team.
sections.avoid: A paragraph that hides the facts.

sections.job: State the problem and the constraint in 2 short paragraphs, from the client's point of view.
sections.avoid: Describing the task instead of the problem.

sections.job: Show 3 to 4 decisive steps with an image each, and say what you chose and what you discarded.
sections.avoid: Twenty process screenshots with no explanation.

sections.job: Show the final work large, in the real context, with a consistent image ratio.
sections.avoid: Mockups that hide the actual design.

sections.job: Close the story with 2 or 3 measured results or a quote from the client.
sections.avoid: Claims such as "improved the experience" with no number.

sections.job: Offer the next project and a way to start a conversation.
sections.avoid: Ending on a dead end with no link.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Product page (e-commerce)
recipes.use_when: One product in a shop: the visitor decides to buy or not, and adds it to the cart.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Show the path back to the category.
sections.avoid: A breadcrumb that repeats the page title as a link.

sections.job: Show 4 to 6 photos with zoom, the first one on a plain background and one in use, all with the same ratio.
sections.avoid: One small photo, or a carousel that autoplays.

sections.job: Put the name, price, stock state and the one "Add to cart" button together, beside the gallery.
sections.avoid: Price below the fold, or two buttons of the same weight.

sections.job: Let the buyer choose size or color with visible options, the chosen one marked and the unavailable ones crossed.
sections.avoid: A dropdown for three colors, or an option that fails only after the click.

sections.job: Answer the fear of buying in 3 lines: delivery time and cost, returns, and payment security.
sections.avoid: Shipping costs that appear for the first time at checkout.

sections.job: Hold the description, specifications and care in tabs or sections after the decision block.
sections.avoid: A wall of marketing text before the specifications.

sections.job: Show the average rating, the count and 3 recent reviews with the buyer's name.
sections.avoid: Only five-star reviews, or reviews with no date.

sections.job: Offer 4 products that complete or replace this one.
sections.avoid: Random products from the same category.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Category / product listing
recipes.use_when: A grid of products or results with filters, where a visitor narrows down and chooses one.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Show the category name, the result count and the path back.
sections.avoid: No count, so the visitor does not know how many items match.

sections.job: Offer the 4 to 6 filters that decide the choice, with the applied ones shown as removable chips.
sections.avoid: Twelve filters open at once, or filters that reload the whole page.

sections.job: Let the visitor sort by relevance, price and newest, with the current choice visible.
sections.avoid: A sort control that does not say what is selected.

sections.job: Show products as cards with image, name, price and one badge at most, all with the same ratio.
sections.avoid: Cards of different heights, or price missing from the card.

sections.job: Move through the results with numbered pages that keep the filters.
sections.avoid: Infinite scroll that loses the position when going back.

sections.job: When nothing matches, say so, show the filters that caused it and a button to clear them.
sections.avoid: A blank page with the word "No results".

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.

recipes.name: Checkout
recipes.use_when: The steps from cart to paid order. Nothing else may compete with finishing.

sections.job: Keep only the logo and a link back to the cart: remove the shop menu.
sections.avoid: The full site menu, which gives the buyer ways to leave.

sections.job: Show the 3 steps (contact, delivery, payment) with the current one marked.
sections.avoid: More than 4 steps, or no way to go back.

sections.job: Ask for email and the delivery address with the fewest fields and autocomplete on.
sections.avoid: Asking for a phone, a company and an account password before the first order.

sections.job: Offer the payment methods as visible options and take the card in the secure field of the provider.
sections.avoid: A card field that looks like a plain input, with no padlock or provider name.

sections.job: Show the items, delivery, taxes and the total in a column that stays in view.
sections.avoid: Costs that change after the last step.

sections.job: Remind of the guarantee: secure payment, returns and where to get help.
sections.avoid: A badge strip of ten logos.

sections.job: End with one button that names the action and the total, such as "Pay 48,00 EUR".
sections.avoid: A button that says "Continue" on the last step.

recipes.name: Sign in / sign up
recipes.use_when: A screen where a person logs in or creates an account.

sections.job: Show the logo and one line that says which action this screen is.
sections.avoid: A marketing paragraph above the form.

sections.job: Ask for email and password only, with a visible label, the show-password toggle and one primary button.
sections.avoid: Placeholders as labels, or error messages that appear only after the submit.

sections.job: For sign-up ask the minimum (email and password), and say what happens next.
sections.avoid: A sign-up with seven fields and a terms checkbox pre-ticked.

sections.job: Offer the one or two providers your audience uses, above or below the form, with the same weight.
sections.avoid: Six provider buttons that outweigh the form.

sections.job: Link to the other path (create account or sign in) and to password recovery, in plain text links.
sections.avoid: Hiding "forgot password" so users cannot find it.

sections.job: On wide screens a calm image or a line of social proof beside the form; hide it below md.
sections.avoid: A visual that pushes the form out of the first screen on mobile.

recipes.name: Onboarding
recipes.use_when: The first minutes after sign-up: get the new user to the first success with few choices.

sections.job: Show where the user is in a 3 to 5 step setup, and what is left.
sections.avoid: No progress, so the user cannot tell how long this is.

sections.job: Ask one thing per step with a clear title, so the answer is easy.
sections.avoid: Three questions on one step, or a step that asks what the product could have guessed.

sections.job: When the user picks a goal or a template, show 3 to 4 large cards with a one-line outcome each.
sections.avoid: A dropdown of 12 options.

sections.job: Offer "skip for now" and "back" at every step, as a text link, so nobody is trapped.
sections.avoid: Mandatory steps that could be done later.

sections.job: Confirm what is ready and lead to the first real task with one button.
sections.avoid: A congratulations screen with confetti and no next action.

recipes.name: Dashboard home
recipes.use_when: The first screen of a signed-in user of an application: it answers "what needs my attention today?".

sections.job: Keep the sections of the product one click away: sidebar with 5 to 7 items, current item marked, account menu at the bottom.
sections.avoid: More than 7 top-level items, or a current item that is not marked.

sections.job: Hold what is global to every screen: search, notifications and the account menu, in the same place on every page.
sections.avoid: Page actions in the top bar: they belong to the page header.

sections.job: Say what this screen is, the period shown and the one primary action of the product.
sections.avoid: Three primary buttons in the header.

sections.job: Show the 3 or 4 numbers the user acts on, each with its change against the last period.
sections.avoid: Twelve metrics of equal weight.

sections.job: Show the one trend that matters over time, with a clear title, axis labels and a period switch.
sections.avoid: A chart without units, or four charts at once.

sections.job: List what needs action now: failures, overdue items and approvals, most urgent first.
sections.avoid: Alerts that are only information.

sections.job: Show the latest 5 to 10 events or records with a link to each and to the full list.
sections.avoid: A list with no link to the record.

recipes.name: Data list / table screen
recipes.use_when: A screen listing records of one kind, where a user searches, filters, sorts and opens one.

sections.job: Keep the sections of the product one click away: sidebar with 5 to 7 items, current item marked, account menu at the bottom.
sections.avoid: More than 7 top-level items, or a current item that is not marked.

sections.job: Name the record type with its count and put the one "New ..." action at the right.
sections.avoid: The primary action hidden in a row menu.

sections.job: Give a search field and the 2 to 4 filters used most, with the applied filters shown as chips.
sections.avoid: A filter bar of ten controls that wraps on two lines.

sections.job: Show 5 to 7 columns that identify the record and its state, sortable, with the row opening the detail.
sections.avoid: Every field of the record as a column, or a row that has no click target.

sections.job: When rows are selected, show the bulk actions in a bar and confirm the destructive ones.
sections.avoid: Delete with no confirmation and no undo.

sections.job: Show the range and total, the page size choice and the previous and next pages.
sections.avoid: Page size fixed at 100, so the list is slow and long.

recipes.name: Detail / record screen
recipes.use_when: One record of an application, opened from a list: the user reads it, edits it or acts on it.

sections.job: Keep the sections of the product one click away: sidebar with 5 to 7 items, current item marked, account menu at the bottom.
sections.avoid: More than 7 top-level items, or a current item that is not marked.

sections.job: Show the way back to the list the user came from.
sections.avoid: A back link that goes to the home page.

sections.job: Show the record name, its status and the 1 or 2 main actions, with the other actions in a menu.
sections.avoid: Six action buttons of the same weight.

sections.job: List the key fields as label and value pairs, grouped by meaning.
sections.avoid: A form that looks editable when it is only for reading.

sections.job: Split the rest into 3 to 5 tabs (activity, files, settings) with the current tab in the URL.
sections.avoid: Tabs that hide the main information.

sections.job: Show the history of the record, newest first, with who did what and when.
sections.avoid: A log with no author or time.

sections.job: Keep irreversible actions apart at the bottom and ask for confirmation naming the record.
sections.avoid: Delete as the first button, in the header.

recipes.name: Settings
recipes.use_when: A screen where a user changes preferences, account details and plan.

sections.job: Keep the sections of the product one click away: sidebar with 5 to 7 items, current item marked, account menu at the bottom.
sections.avoid: More than 7 top-level items, or a current item that is not marked.

sections.job: Name the screen and say what can be changed here in one line.
sections.avoid: No title, so the user does not know which settings they are in.

sections.job: Group the settings in 4 to 6 sections (profile, security, notifications, billing, team) with the current one marked.
sections.avoid: One page with 40 settings and no groups.

sections.job: Show each setting with a label, a help line and its current value, and one Save button per group.
sections.avoid: A save button at the bottom of a page that scrolls for 3 screens.

sections.job: Use switches for settings that apply at once and say what each one does.
sections.avoid: Switches that need a save button to take effect.

sections.job: Confirm every change with a short message or toast, and show errors beside the field.
sections.avoid: Saving silently, so the user repeats the action.

sections.job: Put delete account and similar actions last, with a confirmation that names what is lost.
sections.avoid: A red delete button next to the Save button.

recipes.name: Empty / first-run screen
recipes.use_when: A screen of an application that has no data yet: it must lead to the first record, not show an empty box.

sections.job: Keep the sections of the product one click away: sidebar with 5 to 7 items, current item marked, account menu at the bottom.
sections.avoid: More than 7 top-level items, or a current item that is not marked.

sections.job: Show one calm illustration or icon that relates to the missing content, no larger than 240px.
sections.avoid: A large decorative image that is the main thing on the screen.

sections.job: Say what will appear here and why it is empty, in two lines.
sections.avoid: The words "No data" with nothing else.

sections.job: Give one primary button that creates the first record, named with the object, such as "Add your first project".
sections.avoid: Two equal buttons and a link to the docs.

sections.job: Offer a second path for people who want to look first: sample data or a short checklist.
sections.avoid: A checklist of ten items.

recipes.name: 404 / error page
recipes.use_when: A page shown when the address does not exist or something failed: it must get the visitor back on track.

sections.job: Say whose site this is with the logo, give 3 to 5 links and show one filled button for the primary action.
sections.avoid: Eight links and two filled buttons: the visitor cannot tell which one counts.

sections.job: Say what happened in plain words, such as "This page does not exist", and never blame the visitor.
sections.avoid: A joke that hides the fact that the page is missing, or a raw error code alone.

sections.job: Give one button that takes the visitor to the home or to the last useful place.
sections.avoid: Three buttons that all say "Home".

sections.job: Offer a search field or 3 popular links so the visitor can find what they wanted.
sections.avoid: A search that returns another 404.

sections.job: Close the page with the links that did not fit in the header, the legal pages and one way to contact.
sections.avoid: A wall of 40 links that repeats the whole site map.
